prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one ORIGINAL MASTER painting for one Bhagavad Gita verse in a Sanskrit reader. Generate a single PORTRAIT 9:16 image, 1080x1920 or the highest actually supported native portrait resolution close to 9:16. Consistent series style: refined traditional Indian watercolor and restrained gouache on warm ivory handmade paper; fine organic detail, subtle ochre, sage, dusty terracotta and muted indigo; dignified ancient Indian setting, quiet atmospheric daylight. The image must illustrate THIS VERSE'S ACTUAL MEANING. Read the exact source meaning below; derive a concrete, intelligible scene or a restrained symbolic interpretation of that teaching. Never simply paint an unrelated chariot, generic temple or anonymous landscape. Compose one coherent scene, no collage or infographic. Keep important faces, hands, relationships and narrative objects inside the central 70% of width and central 70% of height, surrounded by ample low-detail sky, ground and paper atmosphere. No important subject cut by an edge. This one master must support portrait/landscape phones and tablets through safe proportional fitting. No text of any kind, no verse number, no letters, no Sanskrit/Roman typography, no watermark, no frame, no UI. Text will be rendered separately by the app over the image at a user-adjustable default image opacity of 48%. If Krishna is depicted, maintain a youthful calm blue-skinned figure in muted golden-yellow garments, a restrained peacock-feather crown, no modern jewelry. Arjuna is a dark-haired warrior with a small crown, bow and understated bronze armor. Use them only when the meaning warrants them; the scene or analogy remains verse-specific.  Reference (DO NOT DRAW THIS TEXT): Bhagavad Gītā 1.2. Exact Sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच ।
दृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवानीकं व्यूढं दुर्योधनस्तदा ।
आचार्यमुपसङ्गम्य राजा वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ २ ॥ Exact stored meaning: Sanjaya said: Then King Duryodhana, seeing the Pandava army arrayed in battle formation, approached his teacher Drona and spoke these words. Chapter context: Before combat on Kurukshetra. Depict the described armies, speakers and events precisely. Dhritarashtra is the blind king listening to Sanjaya in the palace; he is NOT physically on the battlefield. Drona is the elderly martial teacher; Duryodhana is the armored Kaurava king in a muted red cloak. When a verse lists names, render a coherent military group or the stated action, never labeled portrait grids. Krishna and Arjuna have not yet begun the philosophical discourse. No active battle unless the verse actually states it. Previous verse context only, do not substitute for the target: Dhritarashtra said: O Sanjaya, assembled on the sacred field of Kurukshetra, eager to fight — what did my sons and the sons of Pandu do? Next verse context only, do not substitute for the target: O Teacher, behold this great army of Pandu's sons, arrayed for battle by your wise disciple, the son of Drupada. Final instruction: center the distinctive content of the TARGET meaning, not the neighboring verses. No fabricated teaching or unrelated religious scene. Owner-authorized phone-first recomposition: make a genuine tall 9:16 watercolor composition, with the natural setting continuing organically through the portrait canvas. Phones are primary; keep the named main speakers large and clear at 320–430 logical pixels. Keep complete heads, crowns, hands, gestures and important narrative objects safely inside quiet margins. Arrange depth vertically, rather than spreading the essential story across a wide panorama. This same single painting will be contained proportionally on tablets and landscape screens; no edge crop, stretching, square inset, added blank bands or second tablet generation. All flags, books and fabrics must have plain unlettered surfaces, no sacred syllables, invented writing, numbers, labels or annotation marks.
review_note: Contact-sheet inspection; conservative full-frame safe region preserves all figures and objects.

entry.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.2: Sanjaya said: Then King Duryodhana, seeing the Pandava army arrayed in battle formation, approached his teacher Drona and spoke these words.
